title: Geneformer identifies cardiac gene targets validated in engineered heart tissues
summary: Geneformer used learned single-cell transcriptome representations to nominate genes affecting cardiac function. Laboratory tests found that loss of the predicted dosage-sensitive candidate TEAD4 reduced contractile stress in cardiac microtissues. In a separate disease-model application, targeting the Geneformer-nominated genes GSN or PLN improved contractile stress in microtissues carrying a TTN truncating mutation. These are same-study findings in engineered cell-derived tissues, not evidence of clinical benefit. The date records the journal online version; an earlier public version was not established in the bounded search.
ai_technology: Geneformer attention-based pretrained transformer; in silico gene perturbation
organization: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Massachusetts General Hospital

evidence.tested: Geneformer-nominated cardiac genes were tested in engineered iPSC-derived microtissues. TEAD4 loss impaired contractile stress; GSN or PLN targeting improved this readout in the TTN-mutant disease model.
evidence.unknown: Clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy and generalization beyond the studied engineered tissues were not established by these experiments. Full supplements and independent replication were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained transformer supplied context-dependent cell embeddings. Simulated gene perturbations prioritized candidates; researchers performed the functional tissue experiments.

source_review.scope: Primary author manuscript: bounded model/in-silico-perturbation Methods, cardiac Results and figures2/6; institutional manuscript and PubMed dates/affiliations. Supplements not fully reviewed.
